STEP 1 - Vessel type. The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no curved inner wall visible. Vessel: square flat plate.

STEP 2 - Scale. The plate spans roughly 430 px across its width (from about x=185 to x=625). No reliable small reference object (fork, almond, etc.) is visible, so I use the plate's typical size. Square plates are 20-30 cm; a common square dinner plate is about 25 cm. Reconciled width: 25 cm, giving about 17 px per cm.

STEP 3 - Food items.

- Brussels sprouts (roasted): about 6-7 halves visible, patch roughly 170 x 130 px, about 10 x 8 cm, footprint ~64 cm2 after the 0.8 factor. Thickness about 2.5 cm (one sprout stacked, mound averages half). Volume ~80 ml, density 0.6 → ~50 g. Add some hidden underneath: ~70 g.
- Zucchini/yellow squash pieces: patch ~120 x 100 px, ~7 x 6 cm, footprint ~34 cm2, thickness ~1 cm → ~34 ml × 0.6 → ~25 g.
- Caesar-style salad with dressing (chopped romaine, cheese shavings, creamy dressing): patch ~300 x 200 px, ~18 x 12 cm, footprint ~170 cm2, thickness ~1.5 cm average → ~250 ml. Raw leafy greens with dressing, treated as mixed at 0.3 g/ml → ~75 g. Add the parmesan shavings and dressing: total ~110 g.
- Rice/grain base with sauce (brown, lightly coated): patch ~220 x 170 px, ~13 x 10 cm, footprint ~104 cm2, thickness ~1 cm → ~100 ml × 0.8 → ~80 g.
- Chicken or tofu pieces (cubed, cream-coated, on right side): patch ~100 x 120 px, ~6 x 7 cm, footprint ~34 cm2, thickness ~1.5 cm → ~50 ml × 1.0 → ~50 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: a rice base lies under the squash and sprouts, already counted above. Total estimated mass ~ 70 + 25 + 110 + 80 + 50 = 335 g, which is a moderate single-serving plate.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Brussels sprouts, roasted with oil: ~90 kcal/100 g
- Yellow squash, cooked: ~25 kcal/100 g
- Caesar salad with dressing and cheese: ~190 kcal/100 g
- Rice with sauce: ~150 kcal/100 g
- Chicken/tofu pieces: ~170 kcal/100 g
